per_function_top: Cortex-M4 -Os: matchhere 72, match 46, matchstar 38 (sum 156; only 3 functions exist). Secondary pike_ll.c: matchhere 72, matchstar 48, match 46 = 166 (M0+ 170, x86-64 277).
excluded_functions: none — all three functions are engine (match = search-anywhere entry point; there is no test/debug/dump code).
libc_deps: none. `arm-none-eabi-nm -u pike.m4.o` prints nothing: no strlen/memcmp/malloc/setjmp; the code walks NUL-terminated char* directly. Same for pike_ll.m4.o.
ram_model: No malloc, no globals (data=0, bss=0), no buffers; pattern is interpreted directly (no compile step). Recursive backtracking. -fstack-usage (M4 -Os): match 16 B, matchhere 4 B, matchstar 16 B. At -Os matchhere->matchhere and matchhere->matchstar compile to tail calls (b.w); only matchstar->matchhere is a real call (bl), so worst-case stack ~ 16 + 20 B per '*' in the pattern; at -O0 (no tail calls) depth is one frame per pattern character. Run time is exponential in the number of stars: 'a*'x20+'b' vs 25 a's did not finish in 5 s on the host (both variants); no corpus case triggered this (timeouts=0).
features_verified: Read from source. IMPLEMENTED: literal byte match; '.' = any single BYTE (also matches newline); '^' only as first pattern char (anchor to text start; literal elsewhere); '$' only as last pattern char (anchor to text end; literal elsewhere, e.g. 'a$b'); 'c*' / '.*' = zero-or-more of ONE preceding char, tried shortest-first (non-greedy: 'a*' on 'aaa' matches empty). API: int match(re,text) -> 1/0 only, no positions. NOT IMPLEMENTED: + ? {n,m}, lazy quantifiers, alternation |, groups ( ) and (?:), captures, [classes]/ranges/negation, any backslash escape (\d \w \s, escaped metachars — backslash is an ordinary literal), case-insensitive flag, UTF-8 (byte-wise), multiline, pattern validation/error reporting (every string is a 'valid' pattern; 'a**' = a* then literal '*'). Secondary 'leftmost longest' matchstar from the same page: greedy with backtracking for the single star, +10 B.
difftest: Driver: engines/pike-tpop/driver.c (41 lines, plain cc). Adaptations because the API is a bare boolean: START = scan matchhere() at each offset (what match() does internally, '^' honoured); END = probe matchhere(P+'$', text[0..e)) over e ascending (mode A, = the 'leftmost, shortest' match this engine actually finds) or descending (mode B, PIKE_LONGEST=1, leftmost-longest); -i emulated by ASCII-lowercasing pattern+text in the driver; captures impossible (only line 1 printed). RESULTS corpus_seed1: mode A: cases=2088 checked=2081 pass=1189 fail=892 timeouts=0. Of the 1189 passes only 312 are correct spans on expected-match cases; 877 are coincidental agreement on 'nomatch' (the unsupported metachar is taken literally and matches nothing). Mode B: pass=1198 fail=883 (321 real spans). Failure classes, mode A: 612 missing backslash escapes (\d \w \s \b, escaped metachars); 140 missing groups/alternation; 69 missing [character classes]; 45 missing + ? {n,m} (incl. lazy); 22 semantics: byte-wise UTF-8 ('.' on 'é' -> [0,1] vs [0,2]); 2 semantics: '.' matches newline; 2 semantics: shortest-first '*' ('a*' on 'aaa' -> [0,0] vs [0,3]); 0 bugs; 0 timeouts. Mode B: same 612/140/69/45, 15 UTF-8, 2 dot-newline, 0 star-semantics. On the 76 corpus cases that use only c . ^ $ * (ASCII, no -i): 72/76 pass in A, 74/76 in B; the 2 residual failures are '.' matching '\n'. -i emulation: 109/212 -i cases pass vs 108 with -i ignored (the rest fail on other missing features). pike_ll.c variant gives identical counts because the driver's end-probing, not matchstar's search order, decides END.
caveats: (1) This is a boolean matcher: it cannot report match start/end or captures; any real embedding must add position tracking, so 156 B is a floor for 'c . ^ $ *' and not directly comparable with engines that return spans. (2) START/END and -i in the difftest come from the driver's wrapping (documented above), not from the engine; without the wrapper the difftest contract cannot be met at all. (3) Backtracking is exponential in the number of '*' (no memoisation); the corpus never hits it, adversarial patterns do. (4) The only edit to the engine source is the added #include line; the wrapper header adds no code. (5) x86-64 text (313) is larger than the ll variant (277) purely due to clang's tail-call/loop layout; irrelevant for the M4 number. (6) Pass counts are dominated by coincidental 'nomatch' agreement; the meaningful figure is 312 (A) / 321 (B) correct spans out of 1202 expected-match cases.
